unitPlan.title: Grandir, changer et célébrer ensemble
unitPlan.bigIdeas: Développer des relations saines et positives

lessons.title: Je grandis chaque jour
lessons.oneGoal: Students understand that growing and changing is natural and positive

decisionPoints.question: How comfortable are students sharing personal growth experiences?
decisionPoints.guidance: If shy: Use photos/drawings first. If eager: Encourage turn-taking.

decisionPoints.question: What visual supports are needed for growth vocabulary?
decisionPoints.guidance: If confusion: Show before/after pictures. If understanding: Add gestures.

decisionPoints.question: How can we make growth tangible for young learners?
decisionPoints.guidance: If abstract: Use height chart, baby shoes. If engaged: Share growth examples.

lessons.opening: Welcome circle: Point to classroom growth chart. Ask 'Est-ce que vous grandissez?' Show height comparison from September photos.
lessons.mainActivity: Growth exploration station: Students compare baby items (small shoes, bottles) with big kid items. Practice saying 'Je grandis' with growth gestures. Create simple growth timeline with pictures.
lessons.closing: Circle time: Each student says one thing they can do now that babies can't. End with growth chant: 'Je grandis, tu grandis, nous grandissons ensemble!'
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students get emotional about being babies: Emphasize how special growing up is. If energy high: Add movement breaks.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students recognize daily changes in themselves (height, skills, knowledge)
lessons.visualSupports: Height chart, before/after photos, growth gestures (hands moving up)

lessons.title: Mes changements spéciaux
lessons.oneGoal: Students identify personal changes they've experienced and feel proud of them

decisionPoints.question: Which students need encouragement to share achievements?
decisionPoints.guidance: If reluctant: Start with simple examples. If confident: Let them model sharing.

decisionPoints.question: How can we celebrate different types of growth?
decisionPoints.guidance: If limited examples: Provide growth cards. If diverse sharing: Celebrate all types equally.

decisionPoints.question: What scaffolding is needed for comparison vocabulary?
decisionPoints.guidance: If struggling with comparisons: Use visual before/after cards. If ready: Practice full sentences.

lessons.opening: Builds on Lesson 1: Review growth chant. Show mystery box with 'special growth moments' cards inside.
lessons.mainActivity: Special changes gallery walk: Students draw or bring photos showing something new they learned this year. Practice 'Je suis fier de...' with proud gesture. Create 'My Special Changes' book page.
lessons.closing: Proud parade: Students walk around room showing their change picture while others cheer. Practice proud feeling gesture together.
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students can't think of changes: Provide suggestion cards. If comparisons become competitive: Focus on individual growth.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Children recognize their own achievements (walking, talking, reading first words)
lessons.visualSupports: Before/after cards, proud gestures (hands on hips, big smile), growth celebration pictures

lessons.title: Célébrer nos familles
lessons.oneGoal: Students appreciate how families celebrate milestones and traditions together

decisionPoints.question: How can we include diverse family structures?
decisionPoints.guidance: If various family types: Use inclusive family cards. If questions arise: Celebrate all family types equally.

decisionPoints.question: What visual supports help explain family celebrations?
decisionPoints.guidance: If confusion about celebrations: Show celebration photo cards. If engaged: Let students share family photos.

decisionPoints.question: How can quiet students share family traditions?
decisionPoints.guidance: If shy about sharing: Offer drawing option first. If verbal: Encourage storytelling with props.

lessons.opening: Builds on Lesson 2: Review proud feelings. Introduce celebration dance moves. Ask 'Comment votre famille célèbre?'
lessons.mainActivity: Family celebration stations: Students rotate through birthday station (party hats), holiday station (decorations), tradition station (cultural items). Practice celebration vocabulary with actions. Create family celebration card.
lessons.closing: Celebration circle: Students share one family celebration using their card. End with group celebration dance combining all cultures represented.
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If student doesn't celebrate certain holidays: Focus on family togetherness. If overwhelming emotions: Provide comfort and alternative activities.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students connect to birthdays, holidays, and special family moments
lessons.visualSupports: Celebration photo cards, party props, cultural items, celebration gestures (clapping, dancing)

lessons.title: Mes souvenirs de bébé
lessons.oneGoal: Students compare their baby selves to now, recognizing tremendous growth

decisionPoints.question: How can students without baby photos participate fully?
decisionPoints.guidance: If no photos available: Use generic baby/child comparison cards. If photos available: Encourage sharing with class.

decisionPoints.question: What support is needed for time comparison vocabulary?
decisionPoints.guidance: If time concepts difficult: Use visual timeline with pictures. If understanding: Practice comparison sentences.

decisionPoints.question: How can we make the growth concept concrete?
decisionPoints.guidance: If abstract concept: Use measuring tape and baby clothes. If concrete understanding: Add specific skill comparisons.

lessons.opening: Builds on Lesson 3: Review family celebrations. Show baby doll and ask 'Qu'est-ce qu'un bébé peut faire?' vs. 'Qu'est-ce que vous pouvez faire?'
lessons.mainActivity: Then and now comparison: Students create two-column poster showing baby abilities vs. current abilities. Use baby items for tactile comparison. Practice time vocabulary with 'avant/maintenant' gestures. Photo storytelling with baby pictures.
lessons.closing: Growth appreciation circle: Each student shares one amazing thing they can do now. Celebrate with 'We've grown so much!' song with actions.
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If emotional about growing up: Emphasize excitement for new abilities. If no baby items: Use classroom supplies for size comparison.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students see baby photos and understand their incredible development journey
lessons.visualSupports: Baby vs. big kid comparison cards, timeline visuals, before/after gesture (small to big)

lessons.title: Mes amis changent aussi
lessons.oneGoal: Students recognize that their friends are also growing and changing

decisionPoints.question: How can students practice noticing positive changes in peers?
decisionPoints.guidance: If focus on negatives: Guide to positive observations. If positive focus: Encourage detailed sharing.

decisionPoints.question: What support is needed for observation vocabulary?
decisionPoints.guidance: If struggling with observation words: Use pointing and looking gestures. If ready: Add descriptive language.

decisionPoints.question: How can we encourage kind observations?
decisionPoints.guidance: If unkind comments: Redirect to growth celebrations. If kind sharing: Model appreciation responses.

lessons.opening: Builds on Lesson 4: Review individual growth. Play 'Spot the Changes' game with classroom photos from beginning of year.
lessons.mainActivity: Friend growth detective: Students work in pairs with observation sheets, looking for positive changes in each other (skills, interests, height). Create 'My Friend is Growing' certificates. Practice compliment vocabulary with kind gesture.
lessons.closing: Friend celebration: Students present certificates to partners. Group chant: 'We're all growing together!' with friendship hand gestures.
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students focus on appearance: Redirect to skills and kindness. If hurt feelings: Focus on positive growth only.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students notice friends' new skills, interests, and physical growth
lessons.visualSupports: Comparison photos, observation picture cards, friendship gestures (high fives, thumbs up)

lessons.title: Mes rêves pour grandir
lessons.oneGoal: Students express hopes and dreams for their future growth

decisionPoints.question: How can students visualize future goals appropriately?
decisionPoints.guidance: If unrealistic dreams: Guide to achievable goals. If no ideas: Provide dream inspiration cards.

decisionPoints.question: What support is needed for future tense concepts?
decisionPoints.guidance: If future tense difficult: Use 'I want to...' format. If understanding: Practice future vocabulary.

decisionPoints.question: How can we make dreams feel achievable?
decisionPoints.guidance: If overwhelming goals: Break into steps. If achievable goals: Celebrate possibility.

lessons.opening: Builds on Lesson 5: Review friend growth. Share teacher's childhood dream and current reality. Ask 'Quels sont vos rêves?'
lessons.mainActivity: Dream visualization: Students create dream boards with pictures/drawings of future goals. Practice dream vocabulary with reaching gestures. Share dreams in small groups. Create 'My Growth Dreams' journal page.
lessons.closing: Dream circle: Students share one dream using 'Je veux...' sentence starter. End with dream-reaching dance (arms stretching up).
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If dreams seem impossible: Focus on learning and trying. If no participation: Offer drawing or pointing options.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students think about what they want to learn or become
lessons.visualSupports: Dream pictures, future visualization cards, reaching and flying gestures

lessons.title: Nos traditions de classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students create and appreciate classroom traditions that bring the community together

decisionPoints.question: Which classroom traditions resonate most with students?
decisionPoints.guidance: If no engagement: Try different tradition types. If high engagement: Build on popular ideas.

decisionPoints.question: How can all students contribute to tradition-making?
decisionPoints.guidance: If some don't participate: Offer various contribution methods. If all engaged: Rotate leadership roles.

decisionPoints.question: What visual supports help explain community concepts?
decisionPoints.guidance: If community concept unclear: Use circle and connection visuals. If understanding: Practice community actions.

lessons.opening: Builds on Lesson 6: Review dreams for growth. Show photos of current classroom traditions. Ask 'What makes our class special together?'
lessons.mainActivity: Tradition creation stations: Students rotate through greeting station (create special handshakes), celebration station (design class cheers), community helper station (establish helping traditions). Vote on favorites to implement daily.
lessons.closing: New tradition inauguration: Practice chosen class tradition together. Create visual reminder poster for daily use.
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If disagreement about traditions: Use voting or rotation system. If too complicated: Simplify to basic actions.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students participate in daily routines and special class celebrations
lessons.visualSupports: Tradition photo cards, community circle visuals, tradition action demonstrations

lessons.title: Capsule temporelle
lessons.oneGoal: Students create a time capsule documenting their current selves for future reflection

decisionPoints.question: What items best represent each student's current interests?
decisionPoints.guidance: If struggling to choose: Provide category suggestions. If many ideas: Help prioritize most important.

decisionPoints.question: How can students understand the time capsule concept?
decisionPoints.guidance: If concept unclear: Use buried treasure analogy. If understanding: Discuss future discovery excitement.

decisionPoints.question: What support is needed for reflection vocabulary?
decisionPoints.guidance: If reflection difficult: Use simple feeling words. If ready: Encourage detailed descriptions.

lessons.opening: Builds on Lesson 7: Review class traditions. Show mystery box and explain time capsule concept with 'message to future you'.
lessons.mainActivity: Time capsule creation: Students choose 3-4 items representing current self (drawing, photo, favorite item, letter to future self). Practice time vocabulary with past/present/future gestures. Seal items in individual containers.
lessons.closing: Capsule ceremony: Students share one item from capsule before sealing. Plan opening date (end of Grade 1). Store ceremonially in special class location.
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If items too large: Provide size guidelines. If emotional about time passing: Focus on exciting future growth.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students preserve current memories and interests to revisit later
lessons.visualSupports: Time sequence cards, treasure chest visuals, past/present/future timeline gestures

lessons.title: Histoires de famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students share and listen to meaningful family stories about growth and milestones

decisionPoints.question: How can students with language barriers participate?
decisionPoints.guidance: If language difficulties: Encourage drawings or simple words. If multilingual: Celebrate all languages shared.

decisionPoints.question: What scaffolding supports story-telling skills?
decisionPoints.guidance: If storytelling challenging: Provide story prompts. If confident storytellers: Encourage detailed sharing.

decisionPoints.question: How can we honor diverse family experiences?
decisionPoints.guidance: If varying family structures: Celebrate all family types equally. If sensitive stories: Provide supportive listening.

lessons.opening: Builds on Lesson 8: Review time capsule excitement. Share teacher's family growth story with photos. Introduce listening posture and storytelling voice.
lessons.mainActivity: Family story sharing circle: Students take turns sharing family stories about milestones (first steps, birthdays, achievements). Use story props or photos if available. Practice listening skills with active listening gestures. Record special stories in class memory book.
lessons.closing: Story appreciation: Students share favorite story they heard. Practice storytelling ending: 'Et voilà mon histoire!' with proud gesture.
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If no family stories: Create classroom family stories. If emotional stories: Provide comfort and redirect to positive aspects.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students learn about family history and meaningful family moments
lessons.visualSupports: Storytelling props, family photo examples, listening gesture cards (ears, eyes, heart)

lessons.title: Mes moments de fierté
lessons.oneGoal: Students identify and celebrate moments when they felt proud of their growth

decisionPoints.question: How can students recognize different types of success?
decisionPoints.guidance: If narrow success view: Provide diverse achievement examples. If broad understanding: Encourage personal reflection.

decisionPoints.question: What support is needed for emotion vocabulary?
decisionPoints.guidance: If emotion words difficult: Use feeling faces and gestures. If ready: Practice emotional expression sentences.

decisionPoints.question: How can quiet students share pride moments?
decisionPoints.guidance: If reluctant to share: Offer drawing or whispering options. If eager: Provide structured sharing time.

lessons.opening: Builds on Lesson 9: Review family stories. Demonstrate proud feeling with posture and expression. Ask 'When do you feel proud?'
lessons.mainActivity: Pride moment gallery: Students create pride moment displays showing times they felt proud of growth (learning to read, helping others, trying something new). Practice pride vocabulary with confident gestures. Create individual pride books with illustrations.
lessons.closing: Pride celebration walk: Students walk proudly around room sharing one pride moment. Group cheer: 'We are proud of our growth!'
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students can't identify pride moments: Provide achievement suggestion cards. If comparing achievements: Focus on individual growth journey.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students connect to learning to ride bikes, helping others, solving problems
lessons.visualSupports: Achievement picture cards, proud expression examples, success celebration gestures

lessons.title: Grandir ensemble à l'école
lessons.oneGoal: Students understand how the school community supports everyone's growth

decisionPoints.question: How can students recognize various forms of school support?
decisionPoints.guidance: If limited awareness: Take school support walk. If good awareness: Discuss specific helper roles.

decisionPoints.question: What examples resonate with their school experience?
decisionPoints.guidance: If disconnected examples: Use their specific school experiences. If relevant examples: Build on familiar situations.

decisionPoints.question: How can we make community support visible?
decisionPoints.guidance: If abstract concept: Create helper role-play activities. If understanding: Practice appreciation expressions.

lessons.opening: Builds on Lesson 10: Review individual pride moments. Take mini school walk, pointing out all the people who help students grow.
lessons.mainActivity: School community appreciation: Students create thank you cards for different school helpers (teachers, principal, custodian, secretary). Practice support vocabulary with helping gestures. Role-play how different people help students learn and grow.
lessons.closing: Helper appreciation: Students deliver thank you cards to school helpers if possible. Practice gratitude expression: 'Merci de m'aider à grandir!'
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If helpers unavailable for cards: Create appreciation wall display. If shy about delivering cards: Teacher can help facilitate.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students recognize teachers, principals, and peers who help them grow
lessons.visualSupports: School helper photos, helping gesture demonstrations, community support visual maps

lessons.title: Célébrer nos apprentissages
lessons.oneGoal: Students recognize and celebrate the learning growth they've made this year

decisionPoints.question: What learning milestones are most meaningful to celebrate?
decisionPoints.guidance: If struggling to identify progress: Use beginning-of-year work samples. If aware of progress: Encourage detailed sharing.

decisionPoints.question: How can students self-assess their progress?
decisionPoints.guidance: If self-assessment difficult: Provide progress checklists. If ready: Use reflection questions.

decisionPoints.question: What supports are needed for academic vocabulary?
decisionPoints.guidance: If academic terms challenging: Use simple learning words. If understanding: Practice progress descriptions.

lessons.opening: Builds on Lesson 11: Review school community support. Show student work samples from September vs. now. Celebrate obvious improvements.
lessons.mainActivity: Learning growth showcase: Students compare their work from beginning of year to current work in different subjects. Create learning progress posters showing improvement. Practice celebration vocabulary with achievement dances. Self-assessment using simple progress indicators.
lessons.closing: Learning celebration parade: Students march around room holding progress posters. Group chant: 'Look how much we've learned!'
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students don't see progress: Point out specific improvements. If overwhelming comparisons: Focus on individual growth journey.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students see improvement in reading, math, social skills, and independence
lessons.visualSupports: Before/after work samples, progress charts, learning achievement celebration cards

lessons.title: Portfolio de croissance
lessons.oneGoal: Students compile evidence of their growth throughout the year in a personal portfolio

decisionPoints.question: Which artifacts best demonstrate each student's growth?
decisionPoints.guidance: If overwhelmed by choices: Provide selection criteria. If good selections: Encourage reflection on choices.

decisionPoints.question: How can students organize their learning evidence?
decisionPoints.guidance: If organization challenging: Provide clear categories. If organized: Add reflection components.

decisionPoints.question: What reflection supports are needed for portfolio creation?
decisionPoints.guidance: If reflection difficult: Use guided questions. If reflective: Encourage detailed explanations.

lessons.opening: Builds on Lesson 12: Review learning celebrations. Introduce portfolio concept as 'special collection of your growth journey'.
lessons.mainActivity: Portfolio assembly: Students select and organize work samples, photos, and reflections showing their year-long growth. Include items from time capsule activity, pride moments, and learning celebrations. Add reflection labels explaining growth shown in each item.
lessons.closing: Portfolio preview: Students share one favorite portfolio item with a partner. Practice portfolio presentation vocabulary for next lesson.
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If too many items: Help students prioritize most meaningful pieces. If missing items: Use photos or recreate simple versions.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students create a keepsake showing their journey from beginning to end of year
lessons.visualSupports: Portfolio organization charts, growth evidence examples, reflection sentence starters

lessons.title: Présentation de croissance
lessons.oneGoal: Students present their growth journey to others, demonstrating confidence in their development

decisionPoints.question: What presentation format works best for each student?
decisionPoints.guidance: If presentation anxiety: Offer partner or small group options. If confident: Encourage individual presentations.

decisionPoints.question: How can nervous speakers be supported?
decisionPoints.guidance: If very nervous: Use show-and-tell format. If mildly nervous: Provide sentence starters and practice time.

decisionPoints.question: What audience is most encouraging for presentations?
decisionPoints.guidance: If peer audience overwhelming: Invite family or older students. If peer audience supportive: Use classmates.

lessons.opening: Builds on Lesson 13: Review completed portfolios. Practice presentation voice and confident posture. Set up supportive audience expectations.
lessons.mainActivity: Growth journey presentations: Students present their portfolios to audience (family, other classes, or peers), sharing their growth story from beginning to end of year. Use presentation supports like sentence starters and visual cues. Audience practices appreciation responses.
lessons.closing: Presentation celebration: Audience members share appreciations for each presenter. Students reflect on pride in sharing their growth journey.
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If student freezes: Offer to present together. If audience disruption: Redirect to appreciation focus.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students practice public speaking while celebrating personal achievements
lessons.visualSupports: Presentation posture reminders, audience listening guides, confidence building gestures

lessons.title: Jeu de mémoire de croissance
lessons.oneGoal: Students reinforce growth vocabulary and concepts through engaging games

decisionPoints.question: Which game format maintains engagement for all learners?
decisionPoints.guidance: If attention waning: Switch between active and quiet games. If high engagement: Continue with popular formats.

decisionPoints.question: How can different ability levels participate successfully?
decisionPoints.guidance: If mixed abilities: Use team format with peer support. If similar levels: Adjust complexity as needed.

decisionPoints.question: What adaptations support diverse learning needs?
decisionPoints.guidance: If learning differences: Provide visual and kinesthetic options. If standard needs: Use established game rules.

lessons.opening: Extension activity building on all previous lessons through interactive vocabulary practice
lessons.mainActivity: Growth vocabulary games rotation: Memory matching with growth concept cards, charades with growth actions, vocabulary bingo with unit terms, 'Simon Says' with growth movements. Students rotate through stations practicing key vocabulary from entire unit.
lessons.closing: Game celebration: Students vote on favorite growth game. Practice all growth vocabulary with actions one final time.
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If games too competitive: Focus on fun over winning. If behavior issues: Take movement breaks.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students play games that reinforce learning in fun, social contexts
lessons.visualSupports: Game instruction pictures, vocabulary action cards, turn-taking visual cues

lessons.title: Art de croissance créatif
lessons.oneGoal: Students express their growth journey through creative art projects

decisionPoints.question: What art materials best support creative expression?
decisionPoints.guidance: If limited materials: Use simple supplies creatively. If many options: Let students choose preferred media.

decisionPoints.question: How can students with different artistic abilities succeed?
decisionPoints.guidance: If varying abilities: Focus on expression over perfection. If all confident: Encourage detailed work.

decisionPoints.question: What connections can be made between art and growth?
decisionPoints.guidance: If connection unclear: Provide growth art examples. If understanding: Encourage symbolic representation.

lessons.opening: Extension activity building on portfolio concept through artistic expression of growth
lessons.mainActivity: Growth art creation: Students create artistic representations of their growth journey using various media (painting growth trees, collage timelines, sculpture of growth stages, handprint art showing progress). Focus on personal expression rather than technical skill.
lessons.closing: Art gallery walk: Students display and appreciate each other's growth art. Practice art appreciation vocabulary.
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If perfectionism issues: Emphasize process over product. If mess concerns: Set clear cleanup expectations.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students use art to communicate feelings and experiences about growing up
lessons.visualSupports: Growth art examples, art technique demonstrations, creative expression encouragement cards

lessons.title: Théâtre de traditions familiales
lessons.oneGoal: Students act out family traditions, deepening understanding of cultural celebrations

decisionPoints.question: How can shy students participate comfortably in drama?
decisionPoints.guidance: If very shy: Offer prop or background roles. If mildly shy: Partner with confident students.

decisionPoints.question: What support is needed for dramatic expression?
decisionPoints.guidance: If drama skills limited: Focus on simple actions and expressions. If dramatic: Encourage detailed character work.

decisionPoints.question: How can diverse traditions be represented respectfully?
decisionPoints.guidance: If cultural sensitivity needed: Research and respect all traditions. If familiar traditions: Encourage authentic representation.

lessons.opening: Extension activity building on Lesson 3 and 9 through dramatic exploration of family traditions
lessons.mainActivity: Family tradition theater: Students work in small groups to act out different family traditions (birthday celebrations, holiday customs, cultural ceremonies). Use simple costumes and props. Practice dramatic expression and cultural appreciation.
lessons.closing: Tradition theater festival: Groups perform for each other. Audience practices respectful appreciation of all cultural traditions.
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If cultural misunderstanding: Provide gentle correction and education. If stage fright: Encourage participation at comfort level.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students embody family celebrations and share cultural practices
lessons.visualSupports: Cultural tradition pictures, dramatic expression examples, costume and prop demonstrations

lessons.title: Livre de classe collectif
lessons.oneGoal: Students collaborate to create a class book celebrating everyone's growth stories

decisionPoints.question: How can all students contribute meaningfully to the book?
decisionPoints.guidance: If varying abilities: Assign roles based on strengths. If all capable: Rotate leadership responsibilities.

decisionPoints.question: What format allows for diverse contribution styles?
decisionPoints.guidance: If different styles: Use mixed media approach. If similar preferences: Build on class strengths.

decisionPoints.question: How can collaboration be structured for success?
decisionPoints.guidance: If collaboration challenging: Use clear role assignments. If good collaboration: Allow creative freedom.

lessons.opening: Extension activity combining elements from multiple lessons into a collaborative celebration
lessons.mainActivity: Class book creation: Students work together to create a collective book about their class growth journey. Each student contributes a page showing their growth, plus group pages about class traditions, friendships, and shared learning. Combine text, drawings, and photos.
lessons.closing: Book dedication ceremony: Students sign the completed class book and decide where it will be displayed or stored for future classes.
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If disagreements about content: Use democratic voting. If varying work quality: Focus on participation over perfection.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students create a lasting record of their shared classroom community growth
lessons.visualSupports: Book examples, collaboration role cards, page layout templates

lessons.title: Fête de croissance
lessons.oneGoal: Students celebrate their growth journey with a culminating community celebration

decisionPoints.question: What celebration elements are most meaningful to students?
decisionPoints.guidance: If various preferences: Include multiple celebration types. If clear favorites: Focus on popular elements.

decisionPoints.question: How can families be included in the celebration?
decisionPoints.guidance: If family participation possible: Invite for special roles. If family unavailable: Focus on classroom community.

decisionPoints.question: What roles allow all students to participate confidently?
decisionPoints.guidance: If varying comfort levels: Offer diverse participation options. If all confident: Encourage leadership roles.

lessons.opening: Extension activity bringing together all unit concepts in a joyful community celebration
lessons.mainActivity: Growth celebration festival: Students host a celebration including displays of growth portfolios, performance of class traditions, sharing of time capsule predictions, presentation of class book, and appreciation ceremony. Include music, food, and decorations representing class growth journey.
lessons.closing: Celebration reflection: Students share favorite moments from celebration and express gratitude for growth journey together.
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If overwhelming logistics: Simplify to manageable elements. If behavior issues: Provide structured celebration roles.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students experience the joy of shared celebration and community recognition
lessons.visualSupports: Celebration planning charts, role assignment cards, festive decorations and displays

lessons.title: Réflexion sur notre voyage
lessons.oneGoal: Students reflect on their complete learning journey and look forward to continued growth

decisionPoints.question: What reflection tools help students process their learning?
decisionPoints.guidance: If reflection challenging: Use picture-based tools. If good reflection: Encourage detailed thinking.

decisionPoints.question: How can students express their future growth goals?
decisionPoints.guidance: If unclear about future: Provide goal suggestion cards. If clear goals: Encourage detailed planning.

decisionPoints.question: What supports help students recognize their transformation?
decisionPoints.guidance: If transformation unclear: Use concrete before/after examples. If aware: Celebrate recognition.

lessons.opening: Final extension activity helping students synthesize all learning and project forward
lessons.mainActivity: Growth journey reflection: Students complete comprehensive reflection on their entire growth journey using pictures, words, and drawings. Create 'Future Me' vision including goals for Grade 2. Write letters to future selves. Practice gratitude for growth journey and excitement for continued growing.
lessons.closing: Journey appreciation circle: Students share one favorite memory from the growth unit and one goal for future growth. End with final group chant: 'We grew, we learned, we celebrated together!'
lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If sadness about unit ending: Focus on continued growth ahead. If difficulty reflecting: Provide guided questions.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Students understand that growth is ongoing and look forward to summer and Grade 2
lessons.visualSupports: Journey timeline, future visualization cards, reflection prompts with pictures
